definition: For nonnegative p,n, P=sum(p), M=sum(n), D=P-M. If D>0 output(p*D/P,0); if D<0 output(0,n*(-D)/M); otherwise zero. Only active rates are included.
value_question: What follows directly from the selected cancellation rule, without adding mechanisms or data structures?

properties.name: Signed aggregate and magnitude
properties.result: Signed aggregate D is preserved; output L1 mass is abs(D).
properties.reason: The surviving rates sum to the signed net magnitude.

properties.name: Within-polarity identity ratios
properties.result: Ratios among nonzero surviving-direction rates are preserved; independent permutations of the two polarity arrays commute with the operation.
properties.reason: One common scalar multiplies the surviving population; no cross-polarity index correspondence is used.

properties.name: Idempotence and positive homogeneity
properties.reason: The first operation leaves only one polarity; multiplying both populations by a common nonnegative scale preserves their relative cancellation.

properties.name: Absolute L1 perturbations are not amplified by cancellation alone
properties.derivation: On P>M, positive-output derivative wrt positive input j is (1-M/P)*delta_ij+p_i*M/P^2; its column sum is1. Derivative wrt any negative input is -p_i/P and has absolute column sum1. The other sign is symmetric. C is continuous at P=M (output tends to zero), including the origin; integrating along the nonnegative-domain line segment gives the global L1 bound.
properties.limit: Relative error in a tiny signed remainder can still be large. Recurrent gain, thresholds and noise outside C may amplify differences; no global network stability claim.

properties.name: Instantaneous active-support ceiling
properties.result: At most60 of the120 cells per dimension can have positive post-cancellation active rates; across614400 cells the ceiling is307200, i.e.50%.
properties.limit: Applies to the selected current-active-rate operation, not predictive readiness or temporal coverage; positive thresholds can lower the count further.

grouping_counterexample.consequence: Canceling partial contributions in sequence can change contextual cell ratios even when the signed total matches. The semantic boundary must precede any batching/reordering optimization.
grouping_counterexample.scope: Own exact-real arithmetic example; no packet order, frame duration or transfer ordering chosen.

assumptions: Each frame independently supplies positive continuous iid noise to every cell; no learned recurrence or predictive state; no other input.
Activity is counted by strictly positive rate with no threshold or density exclusion. These assumptions are not selected for the model.
exact_consequences: With probability1, totals are unequal and every cell of the winning polarity has positive residual rate. Exactly50% of cells are nonzero each frame, regardless of positive noise amplitude.
By sign symmetry, either whole polarity population wins with probability1/2 per independent frame. Expected cumulative support fraction afterK frames is1-2^(-K).

uniform_noise_mass_approximation.assumption: 60 cells per side, independent Uniform(0,sigma) values.
uniform_noise_mass_approximation.approximation_label: CLT normal approximation, not measured SNN behavior.

dense_positive_noise_comparison.design_implication: Define noise support/distribution and counted activity before choosing a regulator or coverage gate. Dense positive rates with zero-threshold counting would trivially fix occupancy and inflate noise-only coverage; this does not show the specified model fails, because those definitions are open.
dense_positive_noise_comparison.non_goals: No new controller, noise provenance flag, special filter, cutoff, stochastic simulation or state array is introduced.

training_consequence: Because cancellation couples cells within a minicolumn, repair must compare targets with the completed post-cancellation response. Changing one incoming drive can alter other same-dimension outputs; independent uncanceled cell deficits are not automatically the final deficits.

euclidean_error_analysis.definition: C is H-77 proportional population-wide cancellation of two nonnegative m-cell populations. No pairwise matching.

norm_bound.proof: For one minicolumn, output L2 <= output L1 <= input L1 <= sqrt(2*m)*input L2. Sum squared bounds across independent minicolumn blocks to obtain the same whole-CC factor.
norm_bound.sharpness: Take baseline p=(1/2,0,...,0), m_i=1/(2*m); perturb every positive rate by +epsilon and every negative rate by -epsilon. Baseline output is zero. The L2 amplification squared is 2*m*((1/2+epsilon)^2+(m-1)*epsilon^2)/(1/2+m*epsilon)^2, tending to 2*m as epsilon tends to zero from above.
norm_bound.limit: Sharp worst-case bound in Euclidean norm; not a typical noise gain, failure probability or recurrent-network stability result.

focused_vs_broad.premise: Positive total1, negative total1/2, then every negative cell increases by1/10000. Positive cells are either concentrated on one cell or uniform across60. Both cases retain the same signed total and lose the same signed amount.
focused_vs_broad.meaning: Composition is preserved by the cancellation; the same aggregate perturbation is concentrated or spread differently among distinct neuronal rates.

euclidean_error_analysis.validation: All rates, differences and norm squares use exact Fractions. Closed-form near-balance ratio and focused/broad ratios checked independently; square roots are displayed floats.
euclidean_error_analysis.scope: One cancellation operation only. No neuron transfer, background-noise distribution, recurrence, quantizer, controller or error tolerance selected.

post_cancellation_learning.status: conditional one-operation derivative analysis, not a learning algorithm
post_cancellation_learning.value_lineage: C-15/P-29 compares learning objectives; C-18/P-36 constrains them by H77 active-rate cancellation. H74 requires actual value before persistent state.
assumptions: Nonnegative provisional rates, one minicolumn, P=sum(p)>M=sum(m). The opposite branch is symmetric.
A differentiable scalar objective of the post-cancellation rates supplies g_i=dL/dq_i on surviving cells.
Raw rates and source credits are independent inputs for this one-step reference. No recurrence, threshold, teaching or quantized-gradient rule is inferred.
Predictive cancellation is still undecided under H85; the calculation concerns active cancellation or an explicitly chosen later comparison.

identities.sup_norm_bound: max(abs(raw gradients)) <= max(abs(output gradients)) on this branch
identities.signed_net_special_case: For L=ell(P-M), raw positive gradient=ell_prime(P-M) and raw negative gradient=-ell_prime(P-M).
identities.tie: The cancellation map is generally nondifferentiable at P=M. A particular composed loss, such as a smooth signed-net loss, may still be differentiable.

binary32_range_example.consequence: A direct M/P_squared coefficient divides by a zero intermediate although input totals are normal binary32 values.
binary32_range_example.limit: This example does not prove full mixed-precision correctness, especially near a branch boundary.

non_adoptions: No gradient learner, loss, boundary derivative, predictive cancellation or extra state selected.
The within-minicolumn contraction can use transient aggregates; it does not require a stored dense Jacobian.
Whole-sequence credit, nonnegative weight bounds, numerical updates and actual response functions remain separate comparisons.

forward_scaling_arithmetic.status: Two exact-power scalar rounding references; no neuron transition implementation
forward_scaling_arithmetic.value_lineage: H77 makes cancellation the identity for a one-sided active population. C28/P65 and H70 require numerical evaluation to preserve meaningful behavior without unnecessary fields.
forward_scaling_arithmetic.identity: C(p,0)=p for every nonnegative positive-population vector; the current H77 law has D/P=1 in this branch.
assumptions: One nonzero positive rate, no negative rate, finite representable totals.
Round after the indicated operations to binary16 or binary32, nearest ties-to-even with gradual underflow.
Python struct e/f conversions supply the rounding reference; powers-of-two arithmetic before conversion is exact in binary64. No target-device floating-point mode is measured.
forward_scaling_arithmetic.interpretation: The algebraic spelling p_i*D/P is not an instruction-order contract. Forming the bounded common ratio first avoids an unnecessary tiny intermediate product in these cases.
limits: A small ratio, inaccurate totals, final narrow writeback or flush-to-zero behavior still needs separate analysis.
No universal error bound or CPU speed claim; no epsilon floor, lower cutoff, residual field, extra frame or exact format selected.

support_and_magnitude_reference.scope: One algebraic input/cancellation operation on two minicolumns; not a time trajectory or learned DMN state.
assumptions: 60 cells per polarity per coordinate; active rates are nonnegative.
Prior coordinate totals are(1/4,1/4), uniformly distributed across each positive population.
Input coordinate totals are(1/2,-1/2), uniformly distributed across q cells of the corresponding polarity.
Apply H77 to provisional sums; no additional transfer, clipping, noise, learning or phase-state rule.
support_and_magnitude_reference.general_count_identity: For a nonzero coordinate whose prior occupies all m cells of one polarity, a strictly input-winning opposing contribution replaces support m by q input recipients; prior-winning or same-sign input keeps support m. Exact ties remove support; a zero-prior coordinate requires separate accounting.
interpretation: The same input and resulting signed totals can produce different active counts through existing cell participation.
For q=1, summed rate doubles while support falls120→61; for q=60, the same doubled rate leaves support120.
Thus an increase in net-vector L1 does not disprove a drop in active fraction, or establish one. Neither count nor L1 establishes positive residual meaning or later persistence.
support_and_magnitude_reference.non_adoptions: No recruitment quota, activity threshold, semantic label for these vectors, DMN template, controller, new field or preferred H76 branch.
support_and_magnitude_reference.verification: Five exact rational cases; signed totals, summed rate, support counts, rate bound and a nonempty threshold interval checked.

scope_clarifications.clarification: The cumulative support formula concerns fresh noise-only frames without carried activity or other input; equal per-cell distributions give polarity symmetry, and frames are independent. It is not an estimate for a recurrent trajectory with retained state or biased polarity probabilities.
scope_clarifications.effect: Existing assumptions, arithmetic and cases retained; synthesis states the conditional boundary explicitly. No noise process, threshold, classifier or auxiliary structure selected.
